record.paper_title: Regularity of maximal operators: recent progress and some open problems
record.original_question: For 0 <= beta < d, define the centered Hardy-Littlewood fractional maximal operator by M_beta f(x) = sup_{r>0} |B(x,r)|^{beta/d - 1} integral_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy, and define the uncentered version by taking the supremum over balls that contain x. When 0 <= beta < 1 and q = d/(d-beta), is the map f -> |grad M_beta f| bounded from W^{1,1}(R^d) to L^q(R^d)? Does the same endpoint fractional Sobolev bound hold for the uncentered fractional maximal operator?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\geq 1$ be an integer and let $0\leq \beta<d$. For a locally integrable function $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$, define the centered Hardy–Littlewood fractional maximal operator by
$$M_\beta f(x)=\sup_{r>0}|B(x,r)|^{\beta/d-1}\int_{B(x,r)}|f(y)|\,dy,$$
where $B(x,r)$ denotes the open Euclidean ball of radius $r$ centered at $x$ and $|B(x,r)|$ its Lebesgue measure. Define the uncentered version $\widetilde M_\beta f(x)$ by taking the supremum of $|B|^{\beta/d-1}\int_B|f(y)|\,dy$ over all open balls $B\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ containing $x$.

Fix $0\leq \beta<1$ and set $q=d/(d-\beta)$. The questions are:

(a) Is there a constant $C=C(d,\beta)$ such that for every $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ the function $M_\beta f$ is weakly differentiable and
$$\bigl\|\nabla M_\beta f\bigr\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^d)}\leq C\,\|\nabla f\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}?$$

(b) Does the same endpoint inequality hold with $M_\beta$ replaced by the uncentered operator $\widetilde M_\beta$?
artifact.category_tag: Endpoint Sobolev regularity of maximal operators
artifact.status_search_result: D. Beltran and J. Madrid (arXiv:2010.05561, published in Math. Z. 2022) established the endpoint Sobolev bound for both the centered and uncentered fractional Hardy–Littlewood maximal operators in the regime $0<\alpha<1$, $q=d/(d-\alpha)$, settling this question. The result is stated for $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ (and more generally extends to $f\in BV(\mathbb{R}^d)$).

status_evidence.title: Endpoint Sobolev Bounds for Fractional Hardy-Littlewood Maximal Operators
status_evidence.snippet: both the centered and the uncentered Hardy-Littlewood fractional maximal operator M_alpha f are weakly differentiable with ||grad M_alpha f||_{p*} <= C ||grad f||_p ... covers the endpoint case p=1 for 0<alpha<1 where the bound was previously unknown.
status_evidence.claim: Endpoint W^{1,1} -> L^q gradient bound for the centered and uncentered fractional maximal operators is established for 0<alpha<1.

status_evidence.title: Endpoint Sobolev bounds for fractional Hardy–Littlewood maximal operators, Math. Z.
status_evidence.snippet: Published version proving the endpoint Sobolev bound for the centered and uncentered fractional Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator.
status_evidence.claim: The endpoint question is solved in the published Math. Z. paper.
